"""Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3520 (layer 15 MLP down_proj).

What it does: almost nothing. Its causal importance is ~0 at every token (it never
passes the 0.1 threshold in 10M harvested tokens), and switching it off changes the
model's next-token predictions by ~1e-6 nats. Its activation is a dense, noisy
signal (std ~0.27) with no simple token, token-class, or position structure we could
find: token identity explains ~1% of its variance, and coarse token classes (digits,
punctuation, words, newlines) explain ~0.2%.

The one clear regularity: the first token of each document is ~0 (the activation is
0.002 +- 0.002 there), because a document's first token has no context yet. Everywhere
else the activation is noise around its mean, -0.035.

So the program predicts 0 at the first token of each document and the mean elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.035  # the component's mean outside document starts
FIRST_TOKEN_ACTIVATION = 0.0  # a document's first token: ~0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    if starts_doc:
        return carry, FIRST_TOKEN_ACTIVATION
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Sentence-end detector for layer 15, MLP down-projection component 3523.

What it does: it is switched on at the full stop (or ? ! 。？！) that closes a
sentence of ordinary prose, and it grows with how long that sentence has been:
a short sentence gives a weak response, a sentence of about 15 or more words
gives the full response. Stops that close a number (a decimal point after a
digit) or an initial/abbreviation ("J.", "Mr.") respond weakly. All other
tokens are predicted at 0.

Why: measured on training rows, this component is almost silent everywhere else,
and its largest responses are the ends of long declarative sentences in
expository text.
"""

READS = ()

END = set(".?!。？！")
CLOSERS = "\"'”’)]}»*"
PER_WORD = 0.35  # response per word of sentence, before the cap
CAP = 15  # words after which a sentence no longer adds to the response


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: number of words since the last sentence end, newline, or document start
    words = 0 if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        words = 0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    body = tok.rstrip(CLOSERS)
    value = 0.0
    if body[-1:] in END:
        if prev[-1:].isdigit():
            value = 1.0  # decimal point or number
        elif len(prev) <= 2 and prev[:1].isupper():
            value = 0.8  # initial or short abbreviation
        elif prev[-1:].isalpha():
            value = PER_WORD * min(words, CAP)  # end of a prose sentence
        else:
            value = 2.0  # closing quote or bracket after a sentence
        words = 0
    elif "\n" in tok:
        words = 0
    elif tok.strip():
        words += 1
    return words, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3524 (component 3524 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj).

What it is: this component reads essentially one MLP hidden unit (its input vector
is ~0.76 on unit 3524 and small elsewhere), so its activation is that unit's value
scaled by a constant. Its output direction promotes words such as "minor", "tiny",
"modest", "simple" when the activation is negative, and "advanced", "large" when
positive.

What this program does: it predicts the component is pushed negative on words that
mean small, limited or minimal (small, smaller, minor, simple, basic, merely, ...),
the one lexical signal we found, and sits near its typical slightly-negative value
elsewhere. It is a rough description: most of the component's variance is spread
over ordinary text and is not explained by any word list.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words meaning small, limited or minimal in size, amount or degree.
SMALLNESS = frozenset(
    """small smaller smallest little tiny minor modest minimal minimum simple basic
    merely mere short shorter lowest low lower less least fewer few limited slight
    simply""".split()
)

TYPICAL = -0.03  # the component's mean activation
SMALLNESS_VALUE = -0.3  # its mean on these words is about -0.3 to -1.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, SMALLNESS_VALUE if word in SMALLNESS else TYPICAL

"""Activation of one small down_proj component in layer 15 (Qwen3-1.7B MLP).

This component is close to inert. Switching it off changes the model's
next-token predictions by about 2e-6 nats, and it never passes the causal-importance
threshold. Its activation is roughly a symmetric, bell-shaped number with spread 0.36
around 0, and almost none of that spread is explained by the token alone.

This program predicts a small signed value from the kind of the current token:
closing punctuation, quotes, brackets and ellipses tend to be a little negative,
digits and ordinary words a little positive. Each value is the mean activation for
that kind over training rows, so the program is a coarse lookup of the average, not a
mechanism. The first token of a row is always about 0, so it predicts 0 there.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Mean activation per token kind, from training rows (fit by hand from group means).
GROUP_MEANS = {
    "quote": -0.03,
    "ellipsis_or_colon": -0.07,
    "bracket": -0.08,
    "punct": -0.04,
    "newline": -0.01,
    "digit": 0.04,
    "space": 0.02,
    "word": 0.014,
    "other": -0.007,
}


def kind(s):
    """Coarse kind of one token, from its own text."""
    if s.strip() == "":
        return "space"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", s.strip()):
        return "digit"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*[\"“'`]", s):
        return "quote"
    if re.search(r"\.\.\.|^\s*:|:\s*$", s):
        return "ellipsis_or_colon"
    if "\n" in s:
        return "newline"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*[.,;!?:]+", s):
        return "punct"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*[()\[\]{}]+", s):
        return "bracket"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\w+", s):
        return "word"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, GROUP_MEANS[kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3526 (component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3526).

What it does: this component is almost exactly one MLP hidden unit. Its output
direction promotes words such as "itself", "themselves", "direct" and "自身"
(self/direct readings). Its activation is large on words that mean "on one's
own" or "directly, without an intermediary": "directly", "direct", "outright",
"itself", "alone", "individually", "solely", "independently". It is weaker on
looser senses ("separately", "explicitly", "manually", "themselves", "own").
Elsewhere it is a small, diffuse value near its mean (-0.02) that no token rule
captures.

This program reads only the newest token. It returns a high value for the
strong words, a moderate one for the weaker words, and the mean otherwise.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that mean "directly" or "on one's own".
STRONG = {
    "directly", "direct", "outright", "itself", "alone", "individually",
    "solely", "independently", "standalone", "inherently",
}

# Looser senses: separately, explicitly, reflexives, "self" in other languages,
# and other words that single out one thing (only, just, either, else, own).
WEAK = {
    "separately", "separate", "explicitly", "explicit", "exclusively",
    "expressly", "manually", "personally", "themselves", "himself", "solo",
    "only", "just", "either", "else", "own", "individual", "single",
    "simply", "straight", "直接", "本身", "自身", "自己", "mismo", "misma",
    "selbst", "selber",
}

STRONG_VALUE = 1.5
WEAK_VALUE = 0.3
BASE_VALUE = -0.02  # the component's mean activation


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in STRONG:
        return carry, STRONG_VALUE
    if word in WEAK:
        return carry, WEAK_VALUE
    return carry, BASE_VALUE

"""A weak, word-level guess at layer 15 MLP unit 3527 (this component).

What the component does: its activation is mostly small noise around +0.02 (std 0.35),
and almost none of that noise is explained by the current token, the previous tokens, a
bag of recent words, the position in the document, or the local density of math symbols.
Its rare large values are negative: below about -2 on under 0.1% of tokens, and those dips
sit mostly on function words and technical words in informal mathematical reasoning
("there exists a", "for each prime p", "a stack of intervals").

This program keeps only that weak word-level tendency: it predicts a dip on a few
mathematical words and the usual level everywhere else. It explains almost none of the
variance, so it is a placeholder for the component's sign, not a model of it.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.02
DIP = -0.6
MATH_WORDS = {
    "exists", "exist", "prime", "primes", "interval", "intervals", "denominator",
    "exponent", "distinct", "roots", "occurs", "suppose", "assume", "nodes",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position].strip().lower()
    return carry, (DIP if word in MATH_WORDS else MEAN_ACTIVATION)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3528: mostly unexplained by the text.

Its activation is near zero for most tokens, with rare large spikes of both signs that no
simple property of the text predicts. Token identity explains about 2% of its variance (and
a lookup table of tokens is what would be needed to get that); the concepts below explain
well under 1%. What they capture:

- Second token of a document: pushed negative, strongly after a digit-only first token.
- Pronouns (he, she, they, it, its, ...): mildly negative.
- Nouns after a determiner: institutional or event nouns (company, club, team, program,
  system, ...) negative; technical or formal nouns (matrix, vector, triangle, Commission,
  ...) positive.

Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

PRONOUNS = {"he", "she", "they", "it", "them", "its", "his", "her", "their", "him"}
DETERMINERS = {"the", "this", "these", "its", "their", "a", "an", "his", "her", "our", "my", "your"}
INSTITUTIONAL = {"club", "company", "station", "event", "team", "program", "system", "model",
                 "service", "country", "activity", "policy", "league", "tournament", "festival",
                 "organization", "government", "university"}
TECHNICAL = {"matrix", "vector", "triangle", "array", "ratio", "equation", "rate", "energy",
             "potential", "server", "prism", "polygon", "law", "Commission", "Committee", "Republic"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the index of the previous token within its document (None at a row's start)
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    new_doc = carry is None or len(doc) < 2 or doc[-1] != doc[-2]
    index = 0 if new_doc else carry + 1  # this token's position within its document
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    value = 0.0
    if index == 1:
        value = -1.9 if prev.isdigit() else -0.4
    elif word in PRONOUNS:
        value = -0.15
    elif prev in DETERMINERS and not new_doc:
        if word in INSTITUTIONAL:
            value = -0.6
        elif word in TECHNICAL:
            value = 0.5
    return index, value

"""Weak tilt for repeated bigrams.

The component's activation is a diffuse, context-dependent projection of the MLP
hidden state: no token, neighbour or position predicts it well. The one signal we
found is small: a token pair (previous token, this token) that already occurred
earlier in the same document gets a slightly higher mean activation (~0.07) than a
new pair (~0.016). The first token of each document is predicted as 0, where the
component is always near zero.
"""

READS = ()

REPEATED_PAIR = 0.07
NEW_PAIR = 0.016


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the set of token pairs already seen in the current document
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        seen = set()
        return seen, 0.0
    seen = carry
    pair = (prefix.token_ids[-2], prefix.token_ids[-1])
    value = REPEATED_PAIR if pair in seen else NEW_PAIR
    seen.add(pair)
    return seen, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3530: a near-inert, diffuse component.

What it is: a rank-one piece of the MLP down projection. Its activation is
(hidden . V_c) * |U_c|, and V_c is dominated by one MLP hidden unit, 3530 of layer 15
(weight 0.74 of the vector's length; the top 10 units carry 57% of its squared weight).
So its activation is roughly 0.67 times that hidden unit's value, plus a diffuse
contribution from hundreds of other units.

What we could find: its activation has mean about 0.01 and standard deviation about 0.4.
It does not follow token identity (per-token means explain nothing on held-out text),
document position (only the first token of a document sits near 0), or any obvious
context: its strongest positive and negative examples share no lexical or syntactic
pattern. Its causal importance is essentially zero, so switching it off changes the
model's next-token distribution by almost nothing.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean activation at every position.
That is the simplest honest prediction. It explains about 0% of the variance; a
conceptual rule that would do better has not been found.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0101


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's activation at this position: its mean, everywhere."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3531 (the component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3531).

What it is: this component reads one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (about half its
activation's variance is that unit alone). Its value is mostly small noise around 0, with a
heavy negative tail: rare, large negative spikes (down to about -20) in ordinary text, code
and maths alike. Those spikes are not explained by any token class or document type we tried.

What this program does: it predicts the one thing that is consistently visible in the data,
that the strongest-on-average tokens are verbs of intention or expectation ("expected",
"tried", "trying", "need", "should", "want", ...), and the word "to" right after one of them.
Those get a negative value; everything else gets 0.

What it gets: very little. On the eval rows it explains about 0.3% of the variance (Pearson
r about 0.065), and on 4096 training rows about the same. A constant prediction explains none.
The spikes need a finer context than word classes give. A lookup table of per-token means
(held-out) explains about 2%, and a whole-document mean at most about 3%; neither is a
readable concept, so this program does not include one. Its effect on the model's output
is almost the same as switching the unit off.
"""

READS = ()

# Verbs of intention, need and expectation: their next word is often "to", "have" or "be".
EXPECTATION_WORDS = frozenset({
    "expected", "expect", "expects", "tried", "trying", "try", "tries", "want", "wanted",
    "wants", "need", "needs", "needed", "should", "supposed", "required", "asked", "asking",
    "meant", "intended",
})


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    before = _word(prefix.token_strings[-2]) if same_doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if word in EXPECTATION_WORDS:
        value = -0.34
    if before in EXPECTATION_WORDS and word == "to":
        value = -0.4
    return carry, value

"""Activation of MLP hidden-unit readout p-82af68dd L15 down_proj component 3533.

What this component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. It reads the
MLP's 6144 hidden units through a dense direction (its largest single weight is on hidden
unit 3533 itself, but the rest is spread over thousands of units) and writes one direction
into the residual stream. It almost never matters to the output (its causal importance is
~0 everywhere), and its activation has no compact meaning: it is not a clean detector of any
token set, position, document or repeated token. Its activation is roughly zero-mean noise
with a standard deviation of about 0.31.

What this program does: it predicts the activation from the kind of the newest token only.
Whitespace and punctuation sit slightly below zero, words and Han characters a little lower
still, digits at zero. These class means were fitted on training rows; they explain well under
1% of the activation's variance, so this is a weak, readable baseline, not an explanation of
the component's variation. A per-token lookup table would reach only about 3%.
"""

import re

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Mean activation for each kind of token, fitted on training rows.
PUNCT_OR_SPACE = -0.055
WORD = -0.026
DIGIT = 0.0


def kind_value(token: str) -> float:
    """The mean activation of the token's kind: punctuation or whitespace, digits, or words."""
    text = token.strip()
    if text == "" or re.fullmatch(r"\W+", text):
        return PUNCT_OR_SPACE
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", text):
        return DIGIT
    return WORD


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The activation at this position, from the newest token's kind alone."""
    return None, kind_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3534 (a near-dead MLP-output component).

What it does, in plain terms: this component has no readable concept. Its
activation is close to Gaussian noise (std about 0.29, mean about 0.014) and
it is not explained by the current token, the previous token, the position in
the document, or whether the token repeats earlier text. It almost never
matters to the model's output (causal importance is essentially zero at every
token). So the program predicts only the two things that are reliable:

  * exactly 0 at the first token of each document (observed in every case),
  * a small constant, the typical mean activation, everywhere else.

It reads no upstream components and carries no state.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.014  # typical value at non-initial positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A document starts at position 0 of the row, and wherever the document label changes.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or ids[t] != ids[t - 1]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_doc else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3536.

What it does: a weak, diffuse signal that is clearly larger inside runs of
characters that belong to one unit. It is strongest on a digit that follows
another digit (the middle or end of a number such as 2026 or a phone or
reference code), and fairly strong on a Han (Chinese) character that follows
another Han character (the second or later character of a word). Elsewhere it
sits near a small positive baseline, and a digit that starts a number is
slightly negative.

The program is stateless: it looks only at the newest token and the one before
it, within the same document.
"""

import regex

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

HAN = regex.compile(r"\p{Script=Han}")
DIGIT = regex.compile(r"\p{Nd}")

# Typical activation for each case (fit on training text, see explanation).
DIGIT_AFTER_DIGIT = 0.65
HAN_AFTER_HAN = 0.40
DIGIT_STARTING_NUMBER = -0.10
HAN_STARTING_WORD = 0.0
OTHER = 0.05


def is_digit(text):
    return bool(DIGIT.fullmatch(text))


def is_han(text):
    return bool(HAN.fullmatch(text))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    cur, prev = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if is_digit(cur):
        value = DIGIT_AFTER_DIGIT if is_digit(prev) else DIGIT_STARTING_NUMBER
    elif is_han(cur):
        value = HAN_AFTER_HAN if is_han(prev) else HAN_STARTING_WORD
    else:
        value = OTHER
    return None, float(value)

"""Reporting-verb detector (layers.15 MLP down_proj, component 3537).

What it does: this component is positive on a verb of saying that introduces a report of
what someone said or did ("he said", "the speaker mentions", "she told", "explains"), most
strongly when a person is the subject of the verb. It is negative on the word "user" that
opens a user turn in the chat template. Everywhere else it is near zero.

Why these values: on 8k training rows the component's spread is mostly diffuse (no token
class or context explains it), so this program only sketches the large, readable part of
its behaviour: the speech-report tail. Constants are the group means measured there.
"""

READS = ()

# Verbs that introduce reported speech or a statement (inflected forms included).
REPORT_VERBS = frozenset(
    """say says said saying tell tells told telling mention mentions mentioned mentioning
    explain explains explained explaining ask asks asked asking reply replies replied
    answer answers answered warn warns warned claim claims claimed state states stated
    describe describes described announce announces announced comment comments commented
    speak speaks spoke talk talks talked argue argues argued respond responds responded
    insist suggest suggests suggested point points pointed emphasize emphasizes conclude
    concludes advise advises reveal reveals revealed remark remarks remarked""".split()
)

# Words that name who is speaking, when they come right before the verb.
PERSON_SUBJECTS = frozenset("he she i they we you who speaker person".split())

SPEAKER_NOUN = 1.0  # "The speaker ..." (mean 1.0 on its own)
PERSON_REPORT = 1.9  # report verb after a person subject: "he said", "she told"
OTHER_REPORT = 0.3  # report verb in other frames: "it says", "to say"
USER_TURN = -2.1  # the role word "user" after <|im_start|>


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    if cur == "user" and prev == "<|im_start|>":
        return carry, USER_TURN
    if cur == "speaker":
        return carry, SPEAKER_NOUN
    if cur in REPORT_VERBS:
        if prev in PERSON_SUBJECTS:
            return carry, PERSON_REPORT
        if prev.endswith(('"', "”")):  # dialogue tag: '"Hi," she said'
            return carry, 0.0
        return carry, OTHER_REPORT
    return carry, 0.0

"""Predicts a constant for p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3538.

What the component does: almost nothing that can be read off the text. Its activation
(x . V_c) * ||U_c|| is dense and small (RMS about 0.35, but with no sign or size pattern a
reader can name). Measured on 256 training rows (about 131k tokens):
  - the token identity explains no held-out variance (a per-token mean scores below 0),
  - the position in the document, a repeated token, and document-level averages explain
    essentially nothing,
  - the component's causal importance never passes the harvest's threshold, so switching
    it off barely changes the model's output.
So the program predicts the component's typical value, a constant, everywhere. It does not
explain the component's variance; it only records its mean level.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation over the training sample checked above (eval reports -0.0164).
MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.012


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return None, MEAN_ACTIVATION

- the start value of a loop counter ("for (i = 0", "for i := 0"): about -12;
- a line or column number in a file reference ("runner.ts:453:1", "at ... line 9"):
  about -4;
- any other number after a colon ("12:30", "index: 3"): about -1;
- the "et" of "et al." (mostly in citations): about -3.

    r"(?:U\.\s?S\.|S\.\s?Ct\.|L\.\s?Ed\.(?:\s?2d)?|F\.\s?(?:\dd|Supp\.?(?:\s?\dd)?)"

LOOP_START_VALUE = -12.0
FILE_LINE_VALUE = -4.0
ET_VALUE = -3.0
COLON_VALUE = -1.0

small (std about 0.30), has mean about -0.012, and is almost never a large, sparse event.

What was tried: token identity (out-of-sample R^2 0.003), token classes such as digits,
punctuation, words and CJK (R^2 about 0.001), previous-token digits, whether a token already
occurred earlier in its document (R^2 0.001), and document position (flat). None of these
describes the component. Its variance is spread over many contexts, and the largest
magnitudes look like a mixed set of contexts, not one concept.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean activation at every position. It
explains almost none of the variance (R^2 about 0), and it leaves the model's output
essentially unchanged, as switching the component off already does.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.012


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's typical activation at this position: a constant."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""A constant predictor for one MLP feature of layer 15 of Qwen3-1.7B.

The component is down_proj component 3579 (layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3579). It is almost
silent: switched off, it barely changes the next-token predictions, and its causal
importance never passes the harvest's threshold. Its activation is a small positive
offset (mean about 0.13) with a wide, token-to-token scatter (standard deviation about
0.55) and occasional large values, up to about 20, on tokens scattered through
expository, educational and licence-style text.

I could not find a simple concept that predicts that scatter. On held-out text, token
identity, the next token, position in the document, and whether the current text copies an
earlier span each explain well under 1% of its variance. Document genre explains more
(about 12% if the genre were known exactly), but it is not readable from the prefix in
any simple rule that I checked. So the program predicts the component's typical value at
every position: the best constant, since it minimises squared error.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = 0.13
"""The mean activation over training text (0.132 over 2M tokens; 0.138 on the eval set)."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's typical activation at every position; no state is carried."""
    return carry, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3580: a "bound / threshold" detector.

What it responds to (from the real activations):
  * Words that open a limit, threshold or exception, on the word itself:
    "than" after more/less/other ("more than", "less than", "no more than"),
    "at least", "exceed(s)", "beyond", "except", "unless", "only", "even", "non-",
    "outside", "less", "within", "before", "below", "above".
  * The space that comes right before a number after such a word ("before [ ]2010",
    "above [ ]30", "top [ ]10", "under [ ]5"): Qwen writes digits as separate tokens,
    so the space is its own token and sits just before the number.
  * Negative: the root of a Java/URL package name after "package" ("package com.x",
    very strong) or "import" ("import com.google", "import org.apache"), and
    similar domain roots such as "br.com" or "fr" in code.
Everything else is near 0. The large diffuse part (small values on common tokens) is not
modelled. A fixed table of values, read from the prefix alone (causal).

Main program: step() looks at the newest token (and the one before it) and returns
the table value for that pattern.
"""

READS = ()

# "than" after one of these is a numeric comparison ("more than 3"); other "than" is weak.
MORE_LESS = {" more", " less", " other", " fewer", " greater", " later", " earlier"}

# Activation on the bound word's own token.
OWN = {
    " exceed": 9.0, " exceeds": 9.0, " beyond": 7.5, " least": 8.0, " except": 5.4,
    " unless": 4.0, " only": 3.8, " even": 3.6, " non": 3.3, " outside": 3.4, " less": 2.6,
    " within": 1.9, " before": 1.7, " below": 1.6, " not": 1.1, " above": 1.0, " more": 0.9,
    " limited": 1.0, " <": 0.5, " >": 3.3,
}

# Activation on the space token that comes after the bound word, before a number.
SPACE = {
    " before": 9.5, " above": 7.9, " below": 6.8, " within": 5.0, " top": 4.2, " under": 4.6,
    " first": 3.9, " after": 3.7, " beyond": 6.5, " least": 2.5, " than": 2.35, " only": 2.1,
    " non": 2.5,
}

# Top-level domain or first package segment, in Java package and import lines.
DOMAIN = {"com", "org", "br", "cn", "io", "net", "fr", "ru"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    bare = raw.strip()
    if raw == " than":
        return carry, (12.0 if prev in MORE_LESS else 2.0)
    if bare in DOMAIN and prev.strip() == "package":
        return carry, -47.0
    if bare in DOMAIN and prev.strip() == "import":
        return carry, -6.0
    if raw == " " and prev in SPACE:
        return carry, float(SPACE[prev])
    return carry, float(OWN.get(raw, 0.0))

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3581, as a readable program.

What the component is: a rank-one write into the residual stream. Its activation is the
strength of that write: a signed number, usually small (typical |value| about 0.3), that
is a weighted sum of layer 15's MLP hidden units, with unit 3581 the largest single term
(correlation about 0.5). Its causal importance never passes the harvest threshold, so the
model hardly depends on it.

What this program captures: the one visible pattern. The value drops well below zero on
speech-attribution words of news reporting ("said", "told", "stated", "statement",
"report", "official"), and sits near its mean elsewhere. Most of the variance depends on
context that the current token does not show, so the program does not predict it.
"""

READS = ()

# Reporting verbs and nouns that introduce a source ("MTA said", "a statement", "told NBC").
ATTRIBUTION = frozenset({"said", "told", "stated", "statement", "report", "official", "added", "wrote"})

BASELINE = 0.02  # the component's mean value
ATTRIBUTION_VALUE = -0.6  # its typical value on those words


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position].strip().lower()
    return carry, ATTRIBUTION_VALUE if word in ATTRIBUTION else BASELINE

"""Word-group rule for component 3582 of layer 15's MLP down projection.

The component is a rank-one piece of down_proj that reads mostly MLP hidden unit
3582 of layer 15 (about 60% of its variance). Its activation is mostly contextual:
token identity, previous token, position and coarse token classes each explain
about 2% of it or less, and it is almost never switched on (CI ~ 0). The clearest
word-level signal: words that name a plurality or a group ("several", "many",
"multiple", "others", "list", "items") push it up on average (mean about 0.4), and
words that pick out one item or add one more ("each", "every", "any", "only",
"additional", "extra", "further", "remaining") push it down (mean about -0.2).
Other tokens sit near the component's average, 0.04.

The program looks at the newest token only and predicts its group's average. It
explains only about 0.1% of the variance on eval, a little more than predicting the
average everywhere. A large token table would add little: a per-token lookup
explains about 2% of the variance on held-out sample rows.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Plurality, groups and quantities: the component leans positive.
MULTIPLE = frozenset({
    "several", "many", "multiple", "numerous", "various", "others", "most", "more",
    "different", "variety", "majority", "plurality", "list", "items", "examples",
    "pairs", "components", "variables", "collection",
})
# One item of a set, or one more: the component leans negative.
SINGULAR = frozenset({
    "each", "every", "any", "only", "additional", "extra", "further", "remaining",
    "certain", "single", "another",
})
REST = 0.04
MULTIPLE_VALUE = 0.4
SINGULAR_VALUE = -0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in MULTIPLE:
        return carry, MULTIPLE_VALUE
    if word in SINGULAR:
        return carry, SINGULAR_VALUE
    return carry, REST

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()
